newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Senate approves re-election amendment.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Senate approves re-election amendment.

text.p: Brazil's Senate gave its second and final approval to a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election next year.
Senators voted 62-14 in favor of the bill, with two abstentions.
The bill now requires only confirmation by a joint session of Congress before becoming law.
That joint session is due to take place at 1900 local time/1800 EDT/2200 GMT Wednesday, government officials said.

The re-election bill would also allow state governors and mayors to run for a second consecutive term. Senators said they would propose that a separate law be prepared to settle whether or not sitting governors and mayors should stand down for a period before running for re-election.
Analysts say many senators will run for state governorships next year and do not relish the prospect of competing against sitting governors.
